added.title: Hospital Director of Biomedical Engineering
added.description:
offers an exciting opportunity to lead clinical technology strategy at a respected Southern California acute care hospital. This high-impact healthcare leadership role combines innovation, operational excellence, and patient-centered service in a fast-growing community. 🏥

The Hospital Director of Biomedical Engineering
will join an organization recognized for its commitment to quality, patient safety, compassionate care, and community health. Supported by strong local partnerships, the hospital continues to advance modern diagnostic equipment, surgical technologies, patient-monitoring systems, and clinical infrastructure while fostering a culture that values innovation, professional growth, and meaningful healthcare achievements.

The Hospital Director of Biomedical Engineering
will report to a senior hospital operations executive and receive support from experienced clinical, administrative, facilities, information technology, and vendor partners. Key responsibilities include biomedical equipment lifecycle management, regulatory compliance, preventive maintenance, capital planning, cybersecurity coordination, staff development, vendor oversight, and technology integration across hospital departments. The Director will collaborate with friendly nurses and a diverse team of physicians, technicians, healthcare professionals, and operational leaders dedicated to safe, reliable patient care.

The Hospital Director of Biomedical Engineering
will enjoy an outstanding Southern California lifestyle with abundant sunshine, mild winters, and convenient access to beaches, mountains, desert recreation, and scenic hiking trails. The region features live concerts, professional sports, celebrated theme parks, museums, shopping destinations, diverse cuisine, farmers markets, and renowned attractions throughout Los Angeles, Orange County, San Diego, and the Inland Empire, creating an appealing balance of career opportunity and year-round recreation.

The Hospital Director of Biomedical Engineering
may earn compensation up to $145,000, along with a full suite of health and retirement benefits designed to support long-term well-being and financial security. Take the next step in biomedical engineering leadership and connect with a Clinical Management Consultants recruiter to discover how this Southern California hospital career can power the future of clinical technology.

added.title: DIRECTOR, DATA AND TECHNOLOGY SERVICES
added.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

MAKE A DIFFERENCE AT OCHIN

OCHIN is a nonprofit leader in health care innovation and a trusted partner to a growing national provider network, delivering the clinical insights and tailored technologies needed to expand patient access, strengthen care teams, and improve the health of rural and medically underserved communities.

We are hiring for a number of new positions to meet increasing demand. When you choose to join OCHIN, you have the opportunity to continuously grow your skills and do meaningful work to help fulfill our vision of good health and well-being for everyone.

At OCHIN, we value the unique perspectives and experiences of every individual and work hard to maintain a culture rooted in our values.

Founded in Oregon in 2000, OCHIN employs a growing virtual workforce of more than 1,200 skilled professionals, working remotely across 49 states. We offer a generous compensation package and are committed to supporting our employees’ entire well-being by fostering a healthy work-life balance and opportunity for professional advancement. We are curious, collaborative learners who strive to live our values every day. OCHIN is excited to support our continued national expansion and the increasing demand for our innovative tools and services by welcoming new talent to our growing team.

Work Authorization

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a permanent basis at the time of application.

This position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship now or in the future. OCHIN does not provide sponsorship for employment-based visas or transfers of existing employment-based visas.

Position Overview

The Director, Data and Technology Services
supports the mission of OCHIN by providing strategic leadership and operational oversight for enterprise data services, data conversion, data extraction, internal tools development, and technology enablement functions. This role is responsible for ensuring technology and data services are aligned with organizational priorities, support member needs, and deliver measurable business value.

The Director leads through managers and senior technical professionals, providing leadership across Data Management, Data Extraction, Data Conversion, Internal Tools Development, and the Technology Enablement & Automation team. This role is expected to move beyond day-to-day management by defining future-state capabilities, developing multi-year strategies, identifying emerging organizational needs, and ensuring technology investments support OCHIN's long-term objectives.

The Director partners closely with executive leadership, business stakeholders, clinical leaders, and technology teams to shape strategy, influence investment decisions, reduce organizational risk, and build scalable capabilities that support future growth.

Essential Duties

Provide strategic leadership across Data Management, Data Extraction, Data Conversion, Internal Tools Development, and Technology Enablement functions.
Develop and execute multi-year roadmaps for enterprise data services, internal applications, automation, analytics enablement, and technology modernization.
Partner with executive, operational, clinical, and technology leaders to identify emerging business needs and translate them into scalable technology and data strategies.
Anticipate future organizational demands, operational risks, technology shifts, and capability gaps, developing plans to address them before they impact business performance.
Establish governance processes for demand management, portfolio planning, prioritization, resource allocation, and investment decisions.
Build organizational capability by developing managers and technical leaders who demonstrate ownership, accountability, innovation, and strategic thinking.
Drive modernization of technologies, processes, operating models, and service delivery approaches to improve scalability, reliability, efficiency, and member value.
Provide executive oversight of enterprise data platforms, reporting services, ETL/ELT and integration services, data conversion operations, data extraction services, internal application development, and automation capabilities.
Establish and monitor performance measures focused on business outcomes, service value, operational maturity, customer satisfaction, and risk reduction.
Lead cross-functional planning and decision-making to align investments, resolve competing priorities, and advance enterprise objectives.
Develop and manage budgets, vendor relationships, technology investments, software licensing, and contracts aligned with long-term organizational strategy.
Foster a culture of strategic thinking, accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement across Data and Technology Services

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in information technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or related field, or equivalent experience preferred - candidates with a bachelor's degree or higher will be given priority.
Ten or more years of progressive leadership experience across technology services, development, analytics, data services, or enterprise systems IS REQUIRED. (Managing director reports (Project/Program or team lead management in not applicable).
Five or more years leading managers and multi-functional technology organizations required
Experience overseeing data platforms, application development, analytics, reporting services, technology operations, or related functions.
Demonstrated success driving organizational transformation, service modernization, operational excellence, and strategic change.
Experience developing technology roadmaps, organizational strategies, and investment plans.
Experience managing budgets, vendors, contracts, software licensing, and technology investments.
Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, business partnership, and strategic planning skills.
Experience in healthcare, healthcare technology, or Epic-related environments preferred; experience in another large scale EHR systems will be considered.

Base Pay Overview

OCHIN uses broadened pay ranges to support equitable and market-aligned compensation practices. The final offer will be based on a variety of factors, including relevant skills, certifications, education, experience, training, responsibilities, internal equity, and market data.

Physical Requirements/Work Environment

Constant interpersonal skills, teamwork, and customer service. Frequent creativity, mentoring, presentations, and teaching. Occasional decision making and independent judgment or action.
Reading, speaking, writing, and understanding English.
While performing the duties of the job, the employee is regularly required to sit for long periods of time; stand and walk; use hands to finger, handle or feel; reach with hands and arms.
This position requires a virtual home-office environment, working remotely and will require that employees be on camera for all virtual meetings
The role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers and mobile devices.
Travel is required to support OCHIN’s business requirements for go-live installations or training which may require travel by air, vehicle, or train.

Work Location and Travel Requirements

OCHIN is a 100% remote organization with no physical corporate office location. Employees work remotely from home and many of our positions also support our member organizations on-site for new software installations. Nationwide travel is determined based on OCHIN business needs. Please inquire during the interview process about travel requirements for this position.

Work From Home Requirements Are

Ability to work independently and efficiently from a home office environment
High Speed Internet Service
It is a requirement that employees work in a distraction free workplace
Travel may be up to 15% nationally for on-site Go Live support based on business requirements for OCHIN

We offer a comprehensive range of benefits. See our website for details: https://ochin.org/career

COVID-19 Vaccination Requirement

To keep our colleagues, members, and communities safe, OCHIN requires all employees—including remote employees, contractors, interns, and new hires—to be vaccinated with a COVID-19 vaccine, as supported by state and federal public health officials, as a condition of employment. All new hires are required to provide proof of full vaccination or receive approval for a medical or religious exemption before their hire date.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veterans/Individuals With Disabilities

This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights notice from the Department of Labor.

added.title: Chief Technology Officer
added.description:
Chief Technology Officer (CTO) — Remote, USA

Company:
Super Hire (Recruiting on behalf of the client)
Location:
Remote — USA
Employment Type:
Full-Time | Executive Leadership

Company Description
Super Hire Staff helps businesses find the right talent quickly and efficiently, offering services from sourcing qualified candidates to full recruitment support. The team focuses on making hiring processes smooth, reliable, and tailored to client needs. By combining expertise in recruitment with streamlined workflows, Super Hire Staff supports organizations in building strong, high-performing teams. The company values professionalism, responsiveness, and long-term partnerships with clients. Joining Super Hire Staff means contributing to a mission-driven organization that improves how companies hire and grow.
Role Description
The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is a full-time remote role responsible for leading Super Hire Staff’s overall technology vision and execution. The CTO will oversee software and product development efforts, guide IT strategy and architectural decisions, and ensure that technology solutions support business goals and scalability. Daily responsibilities include managing technical teams, prioritizing projects, collaborating with executive leadership on product roadmaps, and implementing best practices for security, performance, and reliability. The role also involves evaluating new technologies, optimizing development processes, and aligning technology investments with organizational objectives. The CTO will play a key role in fostering an inclusive, high-performing engineering culture that supports continuous improvement and innovation.

About the Role

Super Hire is recruiting on behalf of its client for an experienced Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
to lead the organization's technology strategy, engineering operations, innovation, and digital transformation initiatives.
The CTO will work closely with executive leadership to align technology investments with business objectives, build scalable technology capabilities, and lead high-performing technical teams.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and execute the organization's overall technology strategy and roadmap.
Lead engineering, software development, infrastructure, data, and technology operations.
Oversee the design, development, deployment, and ongoing improvement of technology products and platforms.
Evaluate emerging technologies and identify opportunities for innovation and operational improvement.
Establish technology standards, architecture principles, development processes, and performance metrics.
Partner with product, operations, sales, marketing, and executive teams to align technology initiatives with business priorities.
Oversee cybersecurity, data protection, system reliability, and technology risk management.
Manage technology budgets, vendors, strategic partners, and resource planning.
Build, mentor, and develop high-performing engineering and technology teams.
Support digital transformation and long-term technology scalability.

Qualifications & Skills

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field; advanced degree is a plus.
Significant leadership experience in technology, engineering, software development, or a related function.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing technology strategies.
Strong understanding of cloud infrastructure, software architecture, cybersecurity, data, and modern development practices.
Experience managing technical teams, budgets, vendors, and cross-functional initiatives.
Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, communication, and leadership skills.
Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud is preferred.
Experience leading technology transformation or scaling technology operations is advantageous.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States.

What the Client Offers

Fully remote executive leadership opportunity.
Competitive executive compensation package.
Performance-based incentives, where applicable.
Benefits package, where applicable.
Opportunity to shape the organization's technology strategy and innovation roadmap.
Collaborative executive leadership environment.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Super Hire and its client are committed to providing equal employment opportunities. Qualified applicants will be considered based on their qualifications, experience, and business needs without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

How to Apply

Please submit your résumé through the Super Hire LinkedIn job posting
.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the next stage of the recruitment process.
